If you wanted to know all the jobs that AI will produce, look no further than cybersecurity. This is going to become one of the biggest investment areas for enterprises going forward. 

And even as the work becomes more agentic and autonomous you will need more talent to point the agents at the most critical work, review findings, patch systems, respond to incidents, and more. 

Lots of opportunity right now for the systems that protect data and enterprises, as well as the professionals that are deploying them and protecting organizations.

It’s going to only get more wild out there.

items.title:
BREAKING:

@AnthropicAI just launched Duet, its always-on personal agent. It’s t…
items.summaryText:
BREAKING:

@AnthropicAI just launched Duet, its always-on personal agent. It’s the first personal agent I’d call a pro tool.

We’ve been testing it for two weeks. I’ve gone from mostly using ChatGPT to roughly 50/50 between ChatGPT and Claude—the most time I’ve spent with Anthropic in close to a year.

• It lives in its own app, separate from Claude, on iOS, Android, and the web. This makes it feel clean and easy to understand.
• It has channels for specific areas of your work and life rather than just a single chat
• It has a todo list so you never lose what you’re working on and you can always see statuses
• It allows you to easily write and edit documents, slides, and more all through the app.
• It’s not a chief of staff yet. It can see the Claude sessions on my computers but can’t direct them. Its email drafts are worse than dot’s, and voice is transcription only—you can’t have a spoken conversation with it.

My verdict: the vibes are good, and I’m opening Duet every day. It’s worth trying.

Check out our agent comparison page: https://t.co/fZyTorNK4p

Full Vibe Check coming soon on @every

metadata.bio: ceo @every | the only subscription you need to stay at the edge of AI

items.summaryZh:
突发：

@AnthropicAI 刚刚推出了 Duet，这是其常驻个人智能体。它是我第一个会称为专业工具的个人智能体。

我们已经测试了两周。我从主要使用 ChatGPT，变成了在 ChatGPT 和 Claude 之间大约各占一半——这是近一年来我在 Anthropic 上花时间最多的一次。

• 它住在自己的独立应用中，与 Claude 分开，支持 iOS、Android 和网页端。这让它显得干净、易于理解。
• 它有针对你工作和生活中特定领域的频道，而不只是一个聊天窗口
• 它有待办清单，所以你永远不会丢失正在做的事，也总能查看状态
• 它让你可以直接通过应用轻松编写和编辑文档、幻灯片等。
• 它还不是幕僚长。它能在我电脑上看到 Claude 会话，但无法指挥它们。它的邮件草稿比 dot 的差，语音只有转写功能——你无法与它进行语音对话。

我的结论：感觉很好，我每天都在打开 Duet。值得一试。

看看我们的智能体对比页面：https://t.co/fZyTorNK4p

完整 Vibe Check 即将在 @every 发布

items.summaryText:

It's so hard to…
items.bodyText:
You need a frontier team.

Here's why.

Every single person in your company is caught in this dilemma.

Do I get my work done or do I stay up to date with AI and figure out what all these new tools and workflows mean for what work I should do?

That's just crazy.

It's so hard to figure out.

Every single company is struggling with this right now.

Because, I mean, on the one hand, you could ignore the frontier and that'll probably work for a little while until you get disrupted by some agent native version of your product that you didn't see coming.

Or you can keep up with the frontier and just chase shiny objects and never build anything that lasts.

The reason why you need a frontier team is it separates things out.

So you get this nice separation of concerns where you're both keeping up with what's going on on the frontier and you're actually getting your work done.

And I had my co-host, Natalia.

Welcome, Natalia.

Hey, Dan.

Good to be here.

Who is our head of enterprise AI adoption.

Come in and do a little bit of digging into our Frontier team.

So we've been running the Frontier team at Every for, I guess, a couple of months now.

And it has been kind of transformative.

And I think Natalia is one of the best people to come in and take a peek and be like, what are we actually doing?

So actually, I might turn the tables a little bit to you because it was your idea to have a frontier team.

Yeah.

I mean, yeah, the frontier team, I think has been a huge unlock and it's because of this separation that, that I've been talking about.

I think there's so many people at every like me who just love playing with new things and that's super important.

But if that's all you're doing, then you're, you're not going to make progress as a business.

Like you actually do need to go execute on products and services, things that people can rely on.

And it felt like we needed to choose one or the other.

Yeah.

either just constantly be playing with new stuff or make a product that we just build once and then we add features to and we support forever.

And the Frontier team was in a sort of an attempt to say, okay, what if we take all the people like me who love all the new stuff and we just unleash us to just run experiments?

And at the low end, the experiments are just, they're just really good content.

They just teach us something interesting and they become good tweets or YouTube videos or anything like that.

And then on the high end, they get pushed up from the frontier into the products that we build, into the services that we offer, without the rest of the company feeling like they always had to be paying attention to every single model that drops in every single new experiment that we're running.

So I felt like it's allowed me and the other people on the frontier team the space to just figure out what the future looks like without forcing that on the rest of the company until it's actually ready for them to pay attention to it.

Now, one of the things that you seem to have figured out pretty early in the formation of the Frontier team is that you wanted to have both pirates and architects.

Can you describe what that is?

I think there's two archetypes that work really well together, pirates and architects.

Pirates are people like me who are just like, I just want to go really fast and I'm going to do stuff that's kind of be a little bit sloppy, but I'm going to try like a billion things in the space of a couple days.

And I'm going to figure out what's useful.

but it's gonna be a mess.

Architects are people who are really good at being like, there's a whole big messy thing

what would it look like to compress it a little bit and form it into a shape that actually works, that we can actually use?

Because what we try to do on the Frontier team is we're experimenting with lots of stuff.

Yeah, I think the most important thing of a Frontier team is that you inspire your team, but also you listen to your team.

If you do a hundred experiments and don't let it land and don't integrate it, it doesn't work.

You need to listen to your team.

get inspired by your team, and then do stuff, and then make sure that some things will be adopted.

So it's really about integration.

Yes, you should be free and have the freedom to do everything, but in the end, it is about integration and actually bringing it back to the actual organization.

So I would urge everyone, make sure people get what you do and don't get overwhelmed, because it's very easy to overwhelm the entire organization by just...

dumping 100 experiments in a channel.

Make sure some stick.

Make sure people understand what you do.

That's your job as a frontier team.

Amazing.

items.title: Cyber is going to be one of the most profound aspects of AI. We now have a tirel…
items.summaryText:
Cyber is going to be one of the most profound aspects of AI. We now have a tireless workforce that can hunt down, discover, patch, or attack any system and software ever created.

We will use agents to identify the long standing risks in existing systems and infrastructure. Attackers will use agents to accelerate the discovery of gaps in environments. We will equally use agents to defend attacks and discover anomalous patterns to better protect our data, and much more.

We’re entering a new cyber regime, and we’ll probably use 100X more tokens on this loop than we’re imagining right now, because we can scan every log, look at every line of code, look through traffic, and process data at a scale that wasn’t comprehensible before.

More than ever, enterprises are going to care deeply about how they manage their networks, systems, software, data, identity, devices, and more. Agents will largely become the solution to these challenges, but they will keep everyone up in the process.

metadata.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

items.summaryZh:
网络安全将成为 AI 最深刻的方面之一。我们现在拥有一支不知疲倦的劳动力，可以追查、发现、修补或攻击任何曾经被创造出来的系统和软件。

我们将利用智能体识别现有系统和基础设施中长期存在的风险。攻击者会利用智能体加速发现环境中的漏洞。我们同样会利用智能体防御攻击、发现异常模式，从而更好地保护我们的数据，以及做更多事情。

我们正在进入一个新的网络空间格局，而且我们在这个循环中使用的 token 可能会比现在想象的还要多 100 倍，因为我们可以扫描每一条日志、查看每一行代码、检查流量，并以过去无法理解的规模处理数据。

企业将比以往任何时候都更关心如何管理自己的网络、系统、软件、数据、身份、设备等。智能体将在很大程度上成为这些挑战的解决方案，但也会在这个过程中让所有人不得松懈。

items.title: I'm still grokking this...but it does feel like it just as fun to make stuff wit…
items.summaryText:
I'm still grokking this...but it does feel like it just as fun to make stuff with AI as it is to "use" it.

My son watched Star Wars (EP IV) for ~3 hours...but then spent ~20 hours making games about what he had seen. 

But weirdly, he only played the games a little bit...he was more interested in just building the game.

As a programmer, I understand parts of this intuitively...the very act of programming is fun (most of the time). And I have always felt bad for people who couldn't experience that joy...

But maybe everyone will now get to experience that?

metadata.bio: General Partner @SPC, Co-Founder @Bevel_Health | Ex: Early Eng @facebook, CTO @Dropbox, Board @Flipkart | Optimist, Builder, Dad

items.summaryZh:
我还在琢磨这件事……但确实感觉，用 AI 做东西和“使用”AI 一样有趣。

我儿子看了大约 3 小时的《星球大战》（第四部）……但随后花了约 20 小时制作以他所看内容为主题的游戏。

但奇怪的是，他只玩了一小会儿这些游戏……他更感兴趣的是把游戏做出来。

作为一名程序员，我凭直觉能理解其中的部分道理……编程这个行为本身就很有趣（大多数时候）。我一直为那些无法体验这种快乐的人感到遗憾……

但也许现在每个人都能体验到这种快乐了？
